summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 10, part 11) in which Posy, a neighbor, shows Lawrence a boarded-up apartment building across the way and describes how residents are taken away by authorities. She argues that everyone is guilty of some minor offense, which is how the system is rigged, and recounts a neighboring family's removal, including a tattooed number on the mother's wrist. Lawrence, who investigates irregularities in data, is rebuffed when he asks what this has to do with the Order, and leaves. The passage closes by introducing background on Zbigniew Krotoski, a New Yorker inducted into the Order four years earlier who is Lawrence's escapee to find.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, neighbor Posy tells Lawrence that everyone is guilty of something, recounting a family's removal before he leaves to find escapee Zbigniew Krotoski.
key_facts: Posy points out an apartment building across the way with broken windows covered in cardboard, saying the residents were taken away the previous week.
Posy says that people taken away become persons of interest and are kept away because authorities always find a reason to do so.
Posy says 'We're all guilty of something, Lawrence. That's how the game is rigged.'
Posy admits she bought a sofa from a cop ten years ago without a receipt or tax collection, which she says technically makes them offenders.
Posy says she overrode the governor on her radiator ten minutes after it was installed by sticking a penny between two contacts.
Posy describes the family across the street as Pakistani, or maybe Sri Lankan or Bangladeshi, and says she often saw the wife at the service laundry.
Posy says she once saw a number tattooed on the wife's wrist when her sleeve rode up.
Posy says that when the family was taken, the wife stood at the window, pounded on it and screamed for help.
Lawrence's job is finding stuff that doesn't belong in the data; he says he doesn't arrest people.
Posy tells Lawrence he is not very good at connecting the dots when he asks what the story has to do with the Order.
Lawrence thanks Posy, puts his glass in the sink, and she wishes him good luck finding his escapee.
Lawrence knows Zbigniew Krotoski was inducted into the Order four years earlier.
Zbigniew Krotoski is a native-born New Yorker.
In his first two years in the Order, Krotoski tried to coax elders into pointless flamewars about the ethics of working for the Securitat.
